sections.html:
Fairfax County is the most populous county in Virginia, a mostly suburban jurisdiction across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. The 2020 census counted 1,150,309 residents on 406 square miles.

The City of Fairfax is the county seat, but under Virginia law it is an independent city and is not part of the county. Falls Church and Alexandria are independent cities too, which is why a Fairfax County tax bill never covers a house inside those city limits. A house with a Fairfax mailing address might be billed by the county or by the City of Fairfax, or carry a Town of Herndon charge on top of the county. Check the name on the bill before you call anyone.

The Department of Tax Administration has collected the Town of Herndon's current real estate tax since a March 8, 2022 agreement, so Herndon owners get one bill that carries both the county and the town charge.

The county lists the 2026 base real estate rate at $1.12 per $100 of assessed value. The same page shows $1.1225 for 2025 and $1.125 for 2024. The Board of Supervisors sets the general rate in early May each year.

Not every parcel pays the same extra charges. Find your parcel's tax district number in the county's assessment lookup, then match it against the 2026 rate chart. The assessment notice also shows which service districts apply.

The county also lists a $959 yearly charge for Springfield Water Service District 3, which runs through December 31, 2032 and serves a small group of homes in the Lincoln-Lewis-Vannoy Conservation District. Commercial transportation and Dulles Rail districts apply to commercial property, not to a typical house.

Fairfax County bills real estate tax in two installments: July 28 and December 5. When a due date lands on a weekend or county holiday, it moves to the next business day, so the December 2026 installment is due Monday, December 7, 2026.

  • End of February: Notice of Real Estate Assessment Change mailed.
  • April 1: deadline for an appeal to the Department of Tax Administration.
  • June 1: deadline for an appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • July 28: first installment due. Bills go out by June 30.
  • December 5: second installment due. Bills go out by November 5.

Taxes must be paid on time or penalties and interest apply, even when an appeal is pending. Call the office for the current penalty figure.

There are three levels. The assessment effective date is January 1, and the county reported an average residential increase of 3.99% for 2026.

  1. Department of Tax Administration review. File by April 1 (postmarked, or 4:30 p.m. if online or by email). Mail goes to 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 357, Fairfax, VA 22035.
  2. Board of Equalization, an independent panel appointed by the Board of Supervisors. File by June 1. Its decisions are final but can be taken to circuit court.
  3. Fairfax County Circuit Court, through an Application for Correction of Erroneous Assessment under Virginia Code 58.1-3984.

An appeal needs a basis in fair market value, lack of uniformity or an error in the property description. Saying the increase is too large in one year is not a legal basis. For a house, bring sales of similar homes or comparables. An agent filing for you needs a signed, notarized authorization letter.

Appraisal staff take calls at 703-222-8234 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Unpaid real estate tax follows the house, because Virginia gives the tax lien priority over other liens until the tax is actually paid. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says the lien comes ahead of any other lien or encumbrance, and that sale proceeds must be applied to taxes and levies on the real estate. It also covers penalties and interest, and puts a further lien on the rents for the current year.

The seller's share of the taxes is prorated by contract. If installments are unpaid at closing, ask the settlement agent how the balance will be handled on the closing statement.

Recordation also has a seller-side cost. Virginia Code 58.1-802 imposes a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration on a deed, paid by the grantor unless the parties agree that the buyer pays some or all of it. The consideration has to be stated on the first page of the deed.

Fairfax County runs tax relief for seniors age 65 and older and for people with disabilities, along with exemptions for disabled service members and certain surviving spouses. Returning applicants renew by May 1, and first-time or hardship applicants can apply through December 31 for the current and one prior year.

A damaged or decayed house has its own route. The county can adjust the assessment when a building is wholly destroyed, or reduced in value below $100 by decay, or impaired by violence by $100 or more, under Virginia Code 58.1-3293. Any adjustment is prorated from the incident until the repair or the end of the year. Send the address or tax map number, a description of the damage, repair estimates if you have them and photographs to the Department of Tax Administration at 703-222-8234.

Look at your latest assessment notice and confirm which district charges apply. Check whether you pay the county, the City of Fairfax or the Town of Herndon, and which installment is paid. Call 703-222-8234 if a figure looks wrong, and ask the settlement agent how the unpaid balance and the grantor tax will show on the closing statement.

If the house is damaged, start the adjustment request before you list. If you would rather not repair it, a direct as-is cash offer skips showings and lender approvals, and any tax owed is paid from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Fairfax County property tax paid once or twice a year?
faqs.a: Twice a year. The first installment is due July 28 and the second December 5, moved to Monday, December 7 in 2026 because December 5 falls on a Saturday.

faqs.q: What is the Fairfax County base real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county lists $1.12 per $100 of assessed value for tax year 2026. Your notice shows any district charges on top.

faqs.q: What are the Fairfax County assessment appeal deadlines?
faqs.a: April 1 for the Department of Tax Administration and June 1 for the Board of Equalization. Keep paying on time while any appeal is pending.

faqs.q: Who collects tax for the Town of Herndon?
faqs.a: Fairfax County's Department of Tax Administration does, under a March 8, 2022 agreement. Herndon owners receive one combined bill for county and town real estate tax.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the Virginia grantor's tax?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays it unless both sides agree that the buyer covers some or all of it. The rate under Virginia Code 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 of consideration.
